title: Grove blocks delegation to a holder's own second wallet unless that wallet is a registered Active Delegate
content:
A.6.1.1.2.3.1.4.2.4 states: "GROVE holders may only assign their voting power to Active Delegates. This also means **Delegators cannot delegate to another wallet they themselves control**, unless it is an Active Delegate wallet."

The second sentence spells out a consequence the first would otherwise leave implicit, and it is the substantive one. Combined with A.6.1.1.2.3.1.4.1 — only Active Delegates can cast votes, and Delegate status is recorded in a public List Of Delegates — the rule means every unit of *delegated* voting power terminates at a wallet that has passed Grove Foundation onboarding and appears in the registry.

What it forecloses is quiet aggregation. In an open delegation system, a party can concentrate voting power across many wallets into one they control without ever appearing as a recognized actor, and the concentration is invisible because the receiving wallet looks like any other holder. Here, concentration by delegation requires becoming a Delegate, which means identity verification, conflict disclosure, sanctions screening, and a public registry entry.

So the rule turns aggregated voting power into a **disclosed status** rather than an emergent property of the token graph. The registry becomes a reliable map of where delegated influence sits.

The cost is a real restriction on ordinary holders: someone who simply wants to vote from a hot wallet while holding in cold storage cannot use delegation to do it. Grove accepts that friction to keep the registry meaningful. And the protection is bounded — nothing here prevents a party from splitting holdings across wallets and voting each directly. What is blocked is concentration *through the delegation mechanism*, which is the part the framework can see and therefore the part it governs.
description: GROVE holders may only delegate to Active Delegates, so voting power either stays in the holder's own wallet or moves to a Foundation-vetted actor
